text:
nisha: heads up — JS quickstart streaming sometimes delivers duplicate tokens after a reconnect. Repro steps in examples/quickstart-stream: start stream, kill client mid-event, reconnect with Last-Event-ID and you sometimes get the last token twice.

tom: can you paste raw frames or a minimal capture?

nisha: pasted raw output — server sent:

id: 9001
data: {"part":"first"}

then later:

id: 9002
data: {"part":"second"}

but the client log shows a single read that contains:\"first
second\" mashed together (no intermediate blank line), then we abort and reconnect with `Last-Event-ID: 9001`. Server resends 9001 and client emits it again.

rick: that sounds like proxy coalescing. nginx/haproxy often merges writes when buffering is on. Also note TLS and OS layers don't preserve chunk boundaries. SSE clients must be robust to merged frames.

tom: which SDK parser are we using in Node? builtin fetch+stream reader?

nisha: yes, example uses fetch -> ReadableStream reader and simple split on `\n\n`. Works in most cases but stalls if a single LF separates events (some clients tolerate single LF). The node stream waits for the double newline which delays delivery and complicates reconnect semantics.

infra-bot: alert: quickstart-stream staging job shows 1.2% reconnect rate for 2026-03-20T09:12:00Z :warning:

tom: two proposals for parity and DX: (1) perform client-side dedupe on reconnect using `id` (keep small LRU/ring of recent ids), (2) implement tolerant parsing that flushes partial events after configurable short timeout (like 50ms) so we don't wait forever for `\n\n`. Make both opt-in toggles so users can pick strict vs tolerant.

rick: agree. Also add integration tests that intentionally split events mid-json and coalesce them to ensure both Node and Go behave the same. Docker compose with nginx and a flush throttle works well for that.

nisha: workaround for now: servers should include an incrementing `seq` field in the JSON and client app can dedupe on that until SDK fix ships. I'll add a short note in quickstart docs.

doc-bot: suggested doc snippet: \"When using middleboxes (nginx/haproxy) that may buffer HTTP responses, enable immediate flush on the server or enable client-side `sse.tolerantNewline` and `sse.dedupe` in the SDK.\"

tom: action items:
- tom: open SDK issues for Node + Go to add `dedupeById` and `tolerantFlushMs` with tests
- rick: add integration harness (nginx/haproxy) and an E2E that simulates abort+reconnect
- nisha: add quickstart example that demonstrates Last-Event-ID resume behavior and a reproducible nginx config
- infra-bot: scan hosted router configs for `proxy_buffering` and report back

nisha: PR coming with nginx repro and a curl script to exercise the edge case (will link here). :thumbsup:

infra-bot: CI queued for branch quickstart/sse-fix (tests running)

tom: once PRs land let's gate an SDK E2E that asserts no duplicate tokens after abort/reconnect. That should prevent regressions and reduce onboarding friction.

nisha: thanks — this should also help other folks who saw the onboarding stream hang on first token. filing: https://git.internal/repo/issue/1299 and PR https://git.internal/repo/pulls/7801
